title: Fireworks by-law review and permit-based system
subtitle: Also: utility billing moving in-house from Electra, optional residential security camera guidelines, and a staff budget award.
overview: The committee's main item was the fireworks by-law review. It recommended that staff create a permit-based by-law to replace the 1993 by-law {{vote:m3}}. Under the staff proposal, consumer fireworks for personal use would no longer be allowed. Larger displays would need a permit, a licensed display supervisor, liability insurance, a safety inspection and an animal safety plan. Several councillors who supported it said they wanted more time. Some who opposed it wanted a less restrictive approach. The matter returns to the committee at the end of October.

The committee also received a report on moving water, wastewater and stormwater billing in-house, as Electra is leaving the utility billing business {{vote:m1}}. Staff expect a higher annual operating cost starting in 2026 and plan to offset some of it through e-billing, efficiencies and possible user fees. Customers on pre-authorized payment will need to set up a new authorization with the city.

The committee recommended that staff create optional guidelines for residential security cameras, rather than regulate them {{vote:m2}}. The committee also recognized finance staff for a national budget presentation award. These are committee recommendations that Council must still adopt.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff create a new permit-based fireworks by-law to replace and repeal the 1993 by-law {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended that staff create optional guidelines for proper use of residential security cameras {{vote:m2}}.
The committee received the report on moving water, wastewater and stormwater billing in-house for information {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Delegates who sell or represent consumer fireworks argued that permits for personal use would go unused and that a ban would push buying to other communities, online or underground. They said education at the point of sale and stronger enforcement would work better. They accepted permits for large displays.

Another delegate urged a total ban, citing harm to wildlife and pets, noise, air and water pollution, and effects on people with PTSD. A delegate also asked that Lunar New Year be added to the allowed days.

Staff and fire services cited fire risk, injuries, and local incidents requiring a fire response. Staff said a permit-only approach would let by-law officers act on discharge anywhere, including private and school property, which the current by-law does not allow.

Councillors asked about the cost and administrative burden of permits, insurance and licensed supervisors, how small neighbourhood gatherings would be treated, permit turnaround, and fines. Staff said they would bring back cost, distance and comparison information.

On billing, councillors asked staff to avoid new fees for residents because Electra is leaving the business, and asked whether stormwater revenue could absorb the added cost. Staff said account set-up fees would apply mainly when properties change hands. They also discussed smart metering and what other municipalities are doing.
